questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

9 + 7 × 5 – 18 ÷ 2 = 3 × 4 – 10 + 45 ÷ 5
questions.solution:
Interchanging the numbers and using BODMAS rule,

Option 1 → 2 and 5

9 + 7 × 2 – 18 ÷ 5 = 3 × 4 – 10 + 45 ÷ 2

9 + 7 × 2 – 3. 6 = 3 × 4 – 10 + 22. 5

9 + 14 – 3. 6 = 12 – 10 + 22. 5

23 – 3. 6 = 34. 5 – 10

19. 4 is not equal to 24. 5

Option 2 → 18 and 45

9 + 7 × 5 – 45 ÷ 2 = 3 × 4 – 10 + 18 ÷ 5

9 + 7 × 5 – 22. 5 = 3 × 4 – 10 + 3. 6

9 + 35 – 22. 5 = 12 – 10 + 3. 6

44 – 22. 5 = 15. 6 – 10

21. 5 is not equal to 5. 6

Option 3 → 9 and 3

3 + 7 × 5 – 18 ÷ 2 = 9 × 4 – 10 + 45 ÷ 5

3 + 7 × 5 – 9 = 9 × 4 – 10 + 9

3 + 35 – 9 = 36 – 10 + 9

38 – 9 = 45 – 10

29 is not equal to 35

Option 4 → 7 and 4

9 + 4 × 5 – 18 ÷ 2 = 3 × 7 – 10 + 45 ÷ 5

9 + 4 × 5 – 9 = 3 × 7 – 10 + 9

9 + 20 – 9 = 21 – 10 + 9

29 – 9 = 30 – 10

20 = 20

Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of Asha and Lata is 5 : 6. If the difference between their ages is 6 years, then what will be Lata’s age after 5 years?

questions.solution:
According to the given information,

The ratio of present ages of Asha and Lata = 5 : 6

Let the ages of Asha and Lata be 5x and 6x respectively. 

Difference between their ages is 6 years

6x – 5x = 6

x = 6

Then,

Asha’s age, 5x = 5 × 6 = 30

Lata’s age, 6x = 6 × 6 = 36

Lata’s age after 5 years = 36 + 5 = 41

Lata’s age after 5 years is ‘41’

Hence, “41” is the correct answer.

questions.question: A person sells an article at 10% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 332 more, he would have made a profit of 20%. What is the original selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A person sells an article at 10% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 332 more, he would have made a profit of 20%. What is the original selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in profit/loss percentages = 20% − (−10%) = 30%.

Given that 30% of Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 332.

Multiplier for Original Selling Price (SP) at 10% loss = 90%.

Since 30% → 332, then 90% → 332 × 3 = 996.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 996.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial loss = 10%, New profit = 20%, Price increase = Rs. 332.

Formulas: SP = CP × (100 ± P/L%)/100 | Profit = SP − CP.

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

⇒ Original Selling Price (SP1) = 100 − 10 = 90 units.

⇒ New Selling Price (SP2) = 100 ± 20 = 120 units.

⇒ Difference (SP2 − SP1) = 120 − 90 = 30 units.

⇒ According to question, 30 units = Rs. 332.

⇒ 1 unit = 332 ÷ 30.

⇒ Original SP (90 units) = (332 ÷ 30) × 90 = 332 × 3 = Rs. 996.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 996.

Additional Information

Base for Profit/Loss

Unless stated otherwise, Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price of the article.

Percentage Gap Method

If an article is sold at x% loss and then at y% profit, the total difference in SP is represented by (x + y)% of the CP.

questions.question: Rs. 4,300 becomes Rs. 4,644 in 2 years at simple interest. Find the principle amount that will become Rs. 10,104 in 5 years at the same rate of interest
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 4,300 becomes Rs. 4,644 in 2 years at simple interest. Find the principle amount that will become Rs. 10,104 in 5 years at the same rate of interest
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 2 years = 4644 − 4300 = ₹344

Interest rate per year = (344 ÷ 2) ÷ 4300 × 100 = 4%

Total interest for 5 years = 4% × 5 = 20%

Amount = 100% + 20% = 120% of Principal

Principal = (10104 ÷ 120) × 100 = ₹8,420

∴ The correct answer is ₹8,420.

Alternate Method

Given:

First case: Principal (P1) = ₹4,300, Amount (A1) = ₹4,644, Time (T1) = 2 years.

Second case: Amount (A2) = ₹10,104, Time (T2) = 5 years, Rate (R) is same.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100]

Calculations:

⇒ Interest (SI1) = A1 − P1 = 4644 − 4300 = ₹344

⇒ R = (SI1 × 100) ÷ (P1 × T1)

⇒ R = (344 × 100) ÷ (4300 × 2) = 344 ÷ 86 = 4%

⇒ Now for the second case, let the Principal be P2.

⇒ 10104 = P2 × [1 + (4 × 5) ÷ 100]

⇒ 10104 = P2 × [1 + 20 ÷ 100] = P2 × 1.2

⇒ P2 = 10104 ÷ 1.2 = 101040 ÷ 12

⇒ P2 = ₹8,420

∴ The correct answer is ₹8,420.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Property

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant for every year as it is always calculated on the original Principal amount.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total interest percentage for 'T' years at 'R%' rate is simply (R × T)%. This is a very useful shortcut for solving Amount-related problems.

Relationship between A and P

Amount = Principal × [(100 + RT) ÷ 100]. This direct relation helps in finding the Principal when the Amount and Rate-Time product are known.

questions.question: The area of ΔABC is 44 cm 2 . If D is the midpoint of BC and E is the midpoint of AB, then the area (in cm 2 ) of ΔBDE is:
questions.questionHtml: The area of ΔABC is 44 cm<sup>2</sup>. If D is the midpoint of BC and E is the midpoint of AB, then the area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of ΔBDE is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Area of ΔABC = 44 cm2

BD = CD

AE = BE

Concept used:

The line segment joining the mid-points of any two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and equal to half of it.

If in two triangles, corresponding angles are equal, then their corresponding sides are in the same ratio (or proportion), and hence the two triangles are similar.

The ratio of areas of two similar triangles is proportional to the squares of the corresponding sides of both triangles.

Calculation:

According to the concept,

DE ∥ AC, and AC = 1/2 × DE

Let BC = 2 unit, and BD = 1 unit

Area of ΔBDE/Area of ΔBCA = (BD/BC)2

⇒ Area of ΔBDE/44 = (1/2)2

⇒ Area of ΔBDE = (1/4) × 44 = 11 cm2

∴ The area of ΔBDE is 11 cm2

questions.questionHtml: If A lies in the first quadrant and 6 tan A = 5, then the value of \(\frac{{8\sin A - 4\cos A}}{{\cos A + 2\sin A}}\) is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given 6 tan A = 5 ⇒ tan A = 5/6.

The expression (8 sin A − 4 cos A) / (cos A + 2 sin A) can be converted to tan A by dividing both numerator and denominator by cos A.

Converted expression = (8 tan A − 4) / (1 + 2 tan A).

Substitute tan A = 5/6: (8 × 5/6 − 4) / (1 + 2 × 5/6) = (20/3 − 4) / (1 + 5/3) = (8/3) / (8/3) = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: 6 tan A = 5 in First Quadrant (all ratios positive).

⇒ tan A = 5/6 = Perpendicular / Base.

⇒ sin A = 5 / √(52 + 62) = 5 / √61

⇒ cos A = 6 / √(52 + 62) = 6 / √61

Calculation:

⇒ Value = [8(5/√61) − 4(6/√61)] / [6/√61 + 2(5/√61)]

⇒ Value = [(40 − 24) / √61] / [(6 + 10) / √61]

⇒ Value = 16 / 16

⇒ Value = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios

tan A = sin A / cos A. This identity is extremely useful for simplifying expressions involving both sine and cosine into a single variable.

Quadrant Rules (ASTC)

In the First Quadrant (0° to 90°), all trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan, etc.) are positive.

Pythagorean Triplets

For any right-angled triangle, h2 = p2 + b2. Common triplets include (3,4,5), (5,12,13), and (8,15,17).

questions.question: In ΔABC, MN∥BC, the area of quadrilateral MBCN = 130 cm 2 . If AN : NC = 4 : 5, then the area of ΔMAN is:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, MN∥BC, the area of quadrilateral MBCN = 130 cm2. If AN : NC = 4 : 5, then the area of ΔMAN is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of sides AN : AC = 4 : (4 + 5) = 4 : 9.

Ratio of areas ΔMAN : ΔABC = 42 : 92 = 16 : 81.

Ratio of Area(ΔMAN) : Area(quadrilateral MBCN) = 16 : (81 − 16) = 16 : 65.

Given 65 units = 130 cm2 ⇒ 1 unit = 2 cm2.

Area of ΔMAN = 16 × 2 = 32 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 32 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: MN ∥ BC, Area(MBCN) = 130 cm2, and AN : NC = 4 : 5.

Formula Used: If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

⇒ In ΔABC, MN ∥ BC, so ΔMAN ∼ ΔABC (by AA similarity).

⇒ Corresponding sides ratio AN / AC = AN / (AN + NC) = 4 / (4 + 5) = 4 / 9.

⇒ Area(ΔMAN) / Area(ΔABC) = (AN / AC)2 = (4 / 9)2 = 16 / 81.

⇒ Let Area(ΔMAN) = 16k and Area(ΔABC) = 81k.

⇒ Area(quadrilateral MBCN) = Area(ΔABC) − Area(ΔMAN) = 81k − 16k = 65k.

⇒ Given 65k = 130 ⇒ k = 130 / 65 = 2.

⇒ Area of ΔMAN = 16k = 16 × 2 = 32 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 32 cm2.

Additional Information

Area of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides, altitudes, or medians.

Thales Theorem (Basic Proportionality Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides, then the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

Similarity via Parallel Lines

Any line segment drawn parallel to the base of a triangle creates a smaller triangle that is similar to the original larger triangle.
